messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike of 429s detected for customer 'Sapphire Systems' on dedicated pool ded-pool-9 — 5xx/429 ratio crossing thresholds for >2m. Pager -> #oncall-sre.
Sam: taking pager, joining. Can someone drop the customer impact details?
Oris: Sapphire CS here — their app started receiving 429s ~ 11:07am UTC, multiple customers inside their org impacted. They're seeing errors on realtime endpoints, rate-limited responses, high retry loops.
Maya: I'm on metrics. Pulse: sustained 429 rate at 18% of requests from ded-pool-9. Tail shows a single tenant id spiking: tenant-834 (not Sapphire tenant). Could be noisy neighbor causing pool-wide backpressure.
Sam: confirm pool id and topology? is tenant-834 colocated with Sapphire on same pool shard?
Devon: yes ded-pool-9 hosts multiple enterprise tenants. Tenant-834 is a partner integration; hitting a sudden burst of short chat requests.
Lina: Lina (AE) — Sapphire contract has emergency-burst allowance but only via manual approval. If we unblock they get immediate relief. We should consider two paths: 1) emergency contract override for Sapphire, diverting capacity; 2) isolate noisy tenant by per-tenant throttle / eviction. Which is least customer-impacting?
Sam: prefer isolating noisy tenant first (less blast radius). Do we have a per-tenant throttling runbook?
Devon: runbook snippet (ops-runbook-tenant-throttle):
```bash
# apply a soft qps cap for 30m
ri admin tenant-rate-limit set --tenant tenant-834 --pool ded-pool-9 --qps 200 --duration 30m --reason "noisy-neighbor emergency"
# or remove tenant from pool (evict) -> fallback to standard routing
ri infra pool-evict-tenant --tenant tenant-834 --pool ded-pool-9 --force --reason "isolate noisy neighbor"
```
Sam: executing throttle command now. Will run in dry-run then commit.
deploy-bot: Received command, validating ACLs... 
deploy-bot: Applied tenant-rate-limit: tenant=tenant-834 pool=ded-pool-9 qps=200 duration=30m by Sam.
Maya: metrics update in 30s — watching token/latency/429 curves.
Oris: pinged Sapphire: please standby while we attempt mitigation, will update in ~10m.
Sam: update: 60s post-throttle — 429 rate for Sapphire dropped from 18% -> 3%. Traffic for tenant-834 dropped sharply.
Lina: good. Do we need to apply emergency-burst for Sapphire now? They might still be under contracted limits vs real demand.
Oris: Sapphire says they can tolerate short degradation if we avoid customer data movement. They prefer we avoid full contract override if isolation fixes it.
Devon: recommendation: keep throttle for 30m, monitor. If error rate stays low, no override. If we see reoccurrence, escalate to contract-burst (AE + finance approval).
Sam: agree. I'll keep oncall watching for next 20m, set an alert if 429 > 5% for >2m.
Maya: posting dashboard links: https://internal.redwood/metrics/ded-pool-9?window=15m and query used: `sum(rate(http_requests{pool=\"ded-pool-9\",code=\"429\"}[1m])) by (customer)`
Oris: Sapphire update at 11:29am UTC — "errors dropped, service is recovering, thanks" :thumbsup:. They ask for a short RCA and whether we can provision permanent isolation.
Lina: I'll open a case and propose Dedicated pool expansion / tenant pinning options. We should also note contract entitlement for emergency-burst in case customer later requests unthrottle.
Sam: logging incident steps. Current mitigation: per-tenant rate-limit applied. No code changes. No failover.
Devon: follow-ups: 1) schedule capacity planning with infra to consider pinning tenant-834 to its own pool or increase pool headroom, 2) if tenant-834 is a partner, flag for product to consider stricter per-tenant safeguards.
Oris: Sapphire requested a post-incident summary and timeline. I'll draft and send after we close.
Sam: removing pager handoff: I'll stay until 12:00 UTC to watch recovery, then hand to next oncall.
deploy-bot: Tenant-rate-limit expiry scheduled at +30m (will auto-remove at scheduled time).
Maya: final metric snapshot at 11:40am UTC: Sapphire 429s down to 1.2% (within SLO). Tenant-834 throughput reduced as expected.
Sam: closing thread for live mitigation: mitigation succeeded, customer confirmed partial recovery. Next steps: create follow-up ticket (ENG-XXXXX) for capacity isolation, schedule postmortem (ops + product + AE).
Oris: thanks team. I'll inform Sapphire and coordinate RFC for permanent change.
Lina: AE note: log contract override details in the case; we didn't need to use emergency-burst.
Sam: resolved for now. If anyone sees regression, re-alert me.
